cohort: The study involved two cases of severe gestational hypertriglyceridemia managed through a multidisciplinary approach and an additional twenty-one cases identified from a systematic review of published reports on regular apheresis for severe gestational hypertriglyceridemia.
finding: Regular apheresis, particularly using a multidisciplinary approach and CFPP, effectively lowered triglycerides in patients with severe gestational hypertriglyceridemia, with CFPP achieving the highest reduction rate, though 17.4% of patients still experienced acute pancreatitis despite treatment.
